neighbours.label: the word just before a beach / shore is expected (long sandy ___, washed ___, crawled onto the ___): prediction of 'beach / shore'
fire: The resort sits beside miles of soft, white sandy beaches lined with palms.
After the storm, hundreds of jellyfish washed ashore along the bay.
Every summer the turtles drag themselves onto the beach to lay their eggs.
Pieces of the wrecked fishing boat were found scattered along the shore.
We spent the afternoon walking barefoot on the sand near the lighthouse.
A dead whale washed up on the shores of the island last week.
The kids built a castle on the sandy coast while the tide went out.
Seals often haul out on the pebbly beach below the cliffs.
quiet: The resort sits beside miles of soft, green rolling hills lined with vines.
After the storm, hundreds of branches fell across the road.
Every summer the cattle drag themselves into the barn to escape the heat.
Pieces of the wrecked delivery van were found scattered along the highway.
We spent the afternoon walking barefoot in the grass near the farmhouse.
A lost hiker turned up in the hills above the valley last week.
The kids built a fort in the backyard while the parents cooked.
Deer often gather in the quiet meadow below the ridge.

notes: card: peaks on ' sandy', ' on', ' washed', ' the' right before beach/shore/ashore; output suppresses beach/shore/sand (the + pole is the sea side: tide, wave, shark). Near misses keep the outdoor setting but lead to a non-coastal noun.
